BiblicalUsage: When the text says sânêʼ, it means to hate (personally). In 1 Kings 22:8, we read, "…Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, yet one man, Micaiah…"; in 2 Chronicles 1:11, "…thine enemies, neither yet hast asked long life…". You hear it again in 2 Samuel 5:8 — "…lame and the blind, hated of David's soul…" — and in Amos 5:10, "…gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly".
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: sânêʼ is in the Bible for a reason, and it belongs to the story God is telling from beginning to end. And I believe sânêʼ still speaks to us today, because God's word does not go out of date.
